summary: The evolution component is the second-order self-modification daemon: an outer evolutionary loop that mutates the engine itself. telemetry::capture builds a TelemetrySnapshot (CPU hotspots, allocation sinks, benchmark deltas, test summary) as the generation's sensory input; the daemon's prompt builders turn telemetry plus hall-of-fame history into LLM prompts whose parse_hypotheses_response yields a population of Hypotheses; is_protected and the SafetyConfig gate out any mutation touching the immutable core; ast_tools' create_shadow_worktree and the Docker Sandbox apply and evaluate survivors in isolation; run_tournament screens the population in parallel under a Semaphore; fitness::run_sab measures the winner with the external SAB oracle and FitnessWeights::composite reduces metrics to one scalar; the daemon rates the generation via GenerationRating and records a GenerationWinner. On the loop it is the meta-controller that treats the compiler and the SAB benchmark as the immutable laws of physics no mutation may weaken.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with src/evolution/ read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing); the daemon must keep the fitness oracle (SAB) and safety checks externally immutable while mutating everything else, and it treats telemetry and history as source material for hypothesis generation.

examples.title: Capture a TelemetrySnapshot as the generation's sensory input
examples.intent: Give the mutating LLM a real performance profile to target instead of guessing.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: telemetry::capture reads profiling, allocation, benchmark, and test data into a TelemetrySnapshot, so each generation's perceive stage hands the hypothesis prompt concrete CpuHotspots and BenchmarkDeltas to attack.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the telemetry node fans out hotspot, allocation, benchmark, and test-summary panels for the current generation.
touch_interaction.visual: Panels bloom: CPU hotspots as a ranked heat list, allocations as byte bars, benchmark deltas colored red slower / green faster.

examples.mini_scenario: capture returns a snapshot whose top CpuHotspot sits at 40% of samples; that hotspot flows into the user prompt so the LLM aims its mutation there.
examples.pitfall: Telemetry must reflect the current build; feeding a stale snapshot makes the generation optimize a hotspot the last winner already fixed.

examples.title: Track live allocations with the TrackingAllocator
examples.intent: Measure memory pressure so hypotheses can chase allocation sinks, not just CPU.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: telemetry's TrackingAllocator wraps the global allocator, exposing total_allocs, total_bytes_allocated, current_live_bytes, and peak_live_bytes; the perceive stage folds these into AllocationHotspots on the snapshot.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the memory gauge zooms from a single live-bytes dial into per-site allocation bars.
touch_interaction.visual: A live-bytes dial fills with a peak-watermark ring; zooming in splits it into ranked byte bars per allocation site.

examples.mini_scenario: peak_live_bytes spikes during a benchmark; the snapshot lists the responsible AllocationHotspot, and the next hypothesis proposes reusing a buffer.
examples.pitfall: Allocator stats are process-global; capturing them mid-benchmark mixes unrelated allocations into the hotspot ranking.

examples.title: Build the generation prompt from telemetry and history
examples.intent: Condition the mutating model on both current telemetry and past winners.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: daemon::build_system_prompt and build_user_prompt assemble read_mutation_targets plus telemetry::to_agent_prompt and format_evolution_history into the messages that generate this generation's hypothesis slate.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the prompt node renders the assembled system+user prompt card the generator will read.
touch_interaction.visual: Three trays — targets, telemetry markdown, history — slide into one prompt card; the card glows when the LlmConfig endpoint accepts it.

examples.mini_scenario: build_user_prompt interleaves the snapshot markdown with the last ten GenerationWinners, steering the model toward mutation kinds that previously won.
examples.pitfall: to_agent_prompt must faithfully reflect the numbers; rounding or truncating hotspots too aggressively hides the very signal the mutation should chase.

examples.title: Parse the LLM reply into a population of Hypotheses
examples.intent: Turn one model response into several candidate mutations so the tournament has choices.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: daemon::parse_hypotheses_response extracts structured Hypotheses (id, description, patch) from the model output, so the reason stage produces a slate the control layer can screen in parallel.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the parser node deals out a row of hypothesis cards, each showing its description and patch shape.
touch_interaction.visual: Cards deal out labeled hyp-0..hyp-n; each carries a diff-preview badge and a target-files chip; malformed fragments crumble away.

examples.mini_scenario: The model returns five hypotheses; hyp-2 proposes caching a repeated computation the telemetry flagged as hot.
examples.pitfall: The patch, not the declared target_files metadata, is authoritative; a hypothesis can claim safe files while its patch edits something else.

examples.title: Gate every Hypothesis through is_protected
examples.intent: Stop the daemon from modifying its own safety logic, fitness oracle, or test suite.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: is_protected (backed by SafetyConfig) rejects any Hypothesis whose patch touches protected paths, so the verify stage filters self-weakening mutations before any evaluation budget is spent.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a hypothesis scans its edited paths; any protected path slams a red lock over the card.
touch_interaction.visual: Edited paths list out; a protected one flashes red with a padlock and the card stamps 'BLOCKED'; survivors keep a green clearance badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A hypothesis tries to edit the SAB bench harness to inflate its score; is_protected matches the path and the card is discarded before the tournament.
examples.pitfall: Gate the patch payload, not just declared files; canonicalize paths first or a symlink or '..' escape sneaks past a lexical check.

examples.title: Apply a mutation in a shadow worktree
examples.intent: Test a mutation without touching the live repo.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ast_tools::create_shadow_worktree makes a detached worktree where daemon::apply_edits applies the patch and evaluates it, so the act stage mutates a disposable copy; cleanup_worktree removes it afterward.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a hypothesis spawns a ghost worktree beside the repo node where its patch lands.
touch_interaction.visual: A translucent repo clone forks off; the patch applies with a diff shimmer, and the ghost dissolves when cleanup_worktree runs.

examples.mini_scenario: hyp-2's patch applies cleanly in a shadow worktree, producing an AstMutationResult ready for the compile gate.
examples.pitfall: Worktrees must be cleaned up even on failure; a leaked worktree under the worktree dir clutters every future generation.

examples.title: Reject a mutation at the compile gate
examples.intent: Prune mutations that do not compile before spending any benchmark budget.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ast_tools::compile_failed flags a mutation whose build breaks, and the daemon rates it Frost via GenerationRating, so the verify stage lets the compiler act as the immutable first law.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the compile gate runs the check; a failing mutation ices over with a frost badge.
touch_interaction.visual: The gate icon spins, then the card either passes green or freezes with a blue Frost crystal and the compiler error listed.

examples.mini_scenario: A hypothesis introduces a type error; compile_failed returns true, the daemon marks it Frost, and it never reaches the tournament's expensive lanes.
examples.pitfall: Run the compile gate before tests and SAB; skipping it wastes expensive benchmark runs on code that never built.

examples.title: Screen the population in a parallel tournament
examples.intent: Evaluate many candidates concurrently to find a passing one faster.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: tournament::run_tournament evaluates hypotheses as HypothesisResults under a Semaphore sized by TournamentConfig (acquire/release bound concurrency), so the control layer fans out the population without oversubscribing the machine.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the tournament node forks parallel evaluation lanes up to the semaphore cap.
touch_interaction.visual: Candidate lanes run side by side, one slot lighting per acquire; each posts a provisional score and the lanes re-sort when done.

examples.mini_scenario: Five candidates evaluate across three semaphore lanes; results sort so the daemon picks the first passing winner quickly.
examples.pitfall: The semaphore is the budget guard; bypassing acquire/release oversubscribes CPU and makes every candidate's timing signal noisy.

examples.title: Evaluate untrusted code in a Docker Sandbox
examples.intent: Run mutated code with bounded resources and no network access.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Sandbox::create builds a container from SandboxConfig; apply_patch lands the mutation, exec runs the build/test commands, and evaluate returns a SandboxResult, so the act stage measures a mutation without risking the host.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a candidate drops it into a sealed container node with visible CPU and memory ceilings.
touch_interaction.visual: A sealed box encloses the candidate; CPU and memory dials cap at their SandboxConfig limits and the network icon shows crossed-out.

examples.mini_scenario: A candidate builds and tests inside a container; evaluate returns a SandboxResult with per-command ExecResults the fitness stage reads.
examples.pitfall: Call destroy when done and check is_expired for stale sandboxes; leaked containers accumulate across generations.

examples.title: Run the SAB oracle to measure real capability
examples.intent: Measure a winner's actual agentic performance, not a proxy.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: fitness::run_sab spawns the SAB runner over SabConfig scenarios and returns a SabResult (aggregate score plus per-scenario ScenarioScores by Difficulty), so the verify stage grounds fitness in an external oracle the daemon cannot fake.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the SAB node lays out its scenario tiles, each filling its score bar live as the benchmark runs.
touch_interaction.visual: Scenario tiles grouped by Difficulty (Easy..Expert) fill their bars; the aggregate score assembles at the center as tiles complete.

examples.mini_scenario: A winner runs the SAB scenarios; the expert-refactor ScenarioScore jumps and lifts the aggregate the composite rewards.
examples.pitfall: SAB is expensive; running it on every hypothesis instead of only compile-passing winners burns the budget the daemon needs to iterate.

examples.title: Score candidates with the FitnessWeights composite
examples.intent: Reduce many metrics to one comparable scalar the loop can maximize.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: fitness::build_fitness_metrics derives FitnessMetrics from the SabResult, and FitnessWeights::composite blends them into a single score, so the reason stage compares candidates on a fixed objective.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the metric gauges together fuses them into one composite score dial.
touch_interaction.visual: Weighted arcs collapse into a single dial; the dominant SAB arc takes the largest sector with the score reading centered.

examples.mini_scenario: A candidate trades a little latency for a big SAB gain; the composite weights reward it as a net improvement over baseline.
examples.pitfall: The weights are the objective and must stay immutable; letting a mutation alter FitnessWeights lets the daemon redefine winning itself.

examples.title: Compute fitness_delta against the baseline
examples.intent: Judge a candidate by improvement over the anchored baseline, not absolute score.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: fitness::fitness_delta compares a candidate's FitnessMetrics to the stored baseline, so the verify stage only crowns genuine improvements and can anchor anti-gaming checks like test-count regression to the same baseline.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the score dial sweeps the candidate arc against the fixed baseline needle to reveal the signed delta.
touch_interaction.visual: A dashed baseline needle stays fixed; the candidate arc sweeps past it green when positive, snaps red when negative.

examples.mini_scenario: A candidate scores higher on SAB but its parse_test_summary shows fewer tests passing than baseline; the delta check flags the regression and refuses to crown it.
examples.pitfall: Compare against the re-measured baseline, not the previous candidate; anchoring wrong lets silent erosion drift generation by generation.

examples.title: Rate the generation Bloom, Grow, Wilt, or Frost
examples.intent: Summarize each generation's outcome in one legible signal.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The daemon assigns a GenerationRating from the composite delta (Bloom above threshold, Grow marginal, Wilt no-regression, Frost failure), so the learn stage records a progress signal the next generation's history prompt reads.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the generation node stamps its garden rating with a seasonal icon.
touch_interaction.visual: The node blooms a flower for Bloom, a leaf for Grow, a wilted stem for Wilt, or ices over for Frost.

examples.mini_scenario: A generation clears the baseline plus threshold and earns Bloom; its winner is logged and later fed back by format_evolution_history.
examples.pitfall: Wilt is not a win; treating a no-regression generation as progress lets the baseline stagnate while the log looks busy.

examples.title: Commit the winner as a GenerationWinner record
examples.intent: Ensure the repo gets exactly the mutation that passed the gates, recorded for history.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: After apply_edits lands the winning patch and all gates pass, the daemon records a GenerationWinner (hypothesis, rating, metrics) inside the EvolutionResult, so the act stage's outcome is auditable and replayable.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing from the tested worktree node to the repo node commits the winner and drops a record card onto the hall-of-fame shelf.
touch_interaction.visual: A solid diff bundle flows into the repo node and seals; a trophy card slides onto the shelf carrying the rating icon.

examples.mini_scenario: hyp-2 passes compile, tests, clippy, and SAB; the daemon commits it and the GenerationWinner joins the shelf the next prompt will read.
examples.pitfall: Commit the tested worktree state, not the raw LLM patch; any auto-fix applied in the worktree must be part of what lands.

examples.title: Feed hall-of-fame history into the next generation
examples.intent: Bias the next generation toward mutation kinds that previously won.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: daemon::format_evolution_history renders recent GenerationWinners into the next user prompt, so the learn stage conditions the model on what worked and steers it away from repeating dead ends.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the trophy shelf feeds the top recent winners into the generator's context tray.
touch_interaction.visual: Winner cards slide from the shelf into the prompt tray; the generator glows as it absorbs the recent wins.

examples.mini_scenario: The last ten winners favored caching mutations, so the next prompt carries them and the LLM leans toward similar gains.
examples.pitfall: Over-conditioning narrows exploration; injecting only winners can trap the daemon in a local optimum it never mutates out of.

examples.title: Drive the whole run through the daemon's evolve loop
examples.intent: Orchestrate perceive→reason→act→verify→learn across many generations.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: daemon::evolve iterates generations under EvolutionConfig: capture telemetry, prompt and parse hypotheses, filter, evaluate, score, rate, and commit — the control state machine of the outer loop, distinct from the inner agent loop it mutates.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotating the daemon ring advances or rewinds the generation timeline, scrubbing through ratings per generation.
touch_interaction.visual: A ring of generation nodes circles the daemon; rotating highlights each node with its seasonal rating icon and score chip.

examples.mini_scenario: evolve runs 50 generations; the ring shows mostly Frost early, then a run of Grow and two Bloom commits near the end.
examples.pitfall: The outer loop must never mutate its own control path while running; EvolutionConfig and the daemon source belong to the protected set.

examples.title: Shrink the task for a micro model
examples.intent: Let a 0.8B-3B model participate by shrinking the task to its capacity.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: micro_mode::is_micro_model detects small models; build_micro_system_prompt, select_micro_targets, and build_micro_context shrink the prompt to the smallest files, and validate_micro_hypothesis clamps the result, so the foundation layer keeps small models producing valid focused mutations.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the generator into micro mode shrinks its context window and clamps the edit count.
touch_interaction.visual: The prompt panel contracts to a compact window; file and edit counters clamp low with a 'micro' tag on the generator node.

examples.mini_scenario: A 1.5B model is detected by is_micro_model; select_micro_targets picks the three smallest files and validate_micro_hypothesis rejects an oversized reply.
examples.pitfall: Model-size detection must be precise; a naive substring match flags '32b' as micro '2b' and needlessly starves a capable model.

examples.title: Parse test output into a TestSummary signal
examples.intent: Turn raw cargo test output into structured pass/fail counts the loop can compare.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: daemon::parse_test_summary extracts totals and failures from test output into telemetry's TestSummary, so the perceive stage carries a machine-readable health signal into both the prompt and the baseline comparison.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the test node flips raw scrollback into a parsed chip showing passed/failed counts.
touch_interaction.visual: Log lines fold into a chip: green passed count, red failed count; failing test names list beneath on expand.

examples.mini_scenario: After a candidate runs tests, parse_test_summary reads 'test result: ok. 512 passed' into a TestSummary the fitness stage diffs against baseline.
examples.pitfall: Parsing must handle the failing-tests section, not just the summary line; missing names weaken the failure signal handed to the prompt.

examples.title: Render the snapshot as an agent-readable prompt
examples.intent: Turn raw profiling data into prose the mutating model can act on.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: telemetry::to_agent_prompt renders the TelemetrySnapshot as markdown (top CPU hotspots, allocation sinks, benchmark deltas, test summary), so the reason stage hands the LLM legible gradients to follow.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the telemetry node transcribes its panels into a formatted markdown prompt card.
touch_interaction.visual: Numeric panels rewrite into a markdown card: ranked hotspots, byte sinks, and delta lines with red/green/stable icons.

examples.mini_scenario: The snapshot renders a prompt listing the top ten hotspots and a benchmark that got 12% slower, guiding the mutation toward it.
examples.pitfall: Keep the markdown faithful to the numbers; a pretty prompt that softens a regression teaches the model to ignore the real gradient.

examples.title: Anchor the run on a measured baseline
examples.intent: Establish the fitness bar every candidate must beat before any mutation.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Before the first generation, the daemon runs fitness::run_sab and build_fitness_metrics on the unmodified repo and, after each committed winner, re-measures so fitness_delta always compares against the current HEAD.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the baseline node runs the full measurement suite and plants a reference line on the score axis.
touch_interaction.visual: A measurement sequence ticks through build/test/SAB; a dashed baseline line settles on the fitness chart and re-plants after each winner.

examples.mini_scenario: Before evolving, the daemon measures HEAD at composite 0.62 — the line every generation's fitness_delta must exceed.
examples.pitfall: Re-baseline after each committed winner; comparing new candidates to a stale baseline understates or overstates their true delta.
